name: A research study
goal: {{question}} Done when REPORT.md says what was planned, what was found, and what it does not show.

template.title: Research study
template.summary: Question, design, a plan fixed in writing before the data, collection, the planned analysis, a critic's reading, and a report.
template.whenToUse: You are running a study of your own and want the plan written down and fixed before you see any data, and a second reader for the design and for the analysis.
template.notFor: Looking through data you already have to see what turns up. That is worth doing, and it is not this: here the plan comes first.

slots.ask: What is the question, in one sentence?
slots.example: Do short daily quizzes raise exam scores in a first statistics course?

slots.ask: What will you measure, and where will the data come from?
slots.example: End-of-term exam scores for two sections of the course, one with quizzes and one without

description: A plan a person follows, with a few steps an agent may take. You state the question, design the study, and lock the design in writing before any data is collected. You collect the data and write the report. An agent may read the design as a critic, may run the analysis that was planned, and reads the analysis as a critic against what was planned. Work comes back twice: the design while it still leaves out what would count against the idea, and the analysis while it departs from the plan without saying so. The gate before collection is the one decision that cannot be quietly taken back: after it, the plan is not edited, and later changes are written beside it with a date. Nothing here needs a coding harness.

nodes.name: State the question
nodes.brief: Write the question in one sentence, why it matters, and what answer would change what you do. If no answer would change anything, say so now.

nodes.name: Design the study
nodes.brief: Say what you will measure and on what, how many, and how you will analyze it. Name in advance the result that would count for the idea and the result that would count against it. If you cannot name one that would count against it, the design is not finished.
outputs: DESIGN.md: the measure, the sample, the analysis, and what would count for and against

nodes.name: A critic reads the design
nodes.brief: Read the design as a skeptic. Can the question be answered by this measure on this sample? Is there a result that would count against the idea, and would the planned analysis show it? What could produce the hoped-for result for another reason? You judge the design and do not rewrite it. Verdict pass only when each of those has an answer in DESIGN.md.
outputs: DESIGN-REVIEW.md: one line per point, and a verdict line

nodes.name: Lock the design
nodes.prompt: Is this the study you will run? Once you say yes, the design is written out as the plan of record and is not edited again.

nodes.name: Write the plan of record
nodes.brief: Copy from DESIGN.md what will be measured, on what and how many, the analysis, and the results that would count for and against. Date it. From here this file is not edited: anything you change later is written beside it as a dated note, with the reason.

nodes.name: Collect the data
nodes.brief: Collect what the plan of record says, as it says. Keep a log as you go: what was collected and when, anything that went differently from the plan, and anything you left out and why.

nodes.name: Run the planned analysis
nodes.brief: Run the analysis the plan of record names, first and as written. Anything else you look at goes in a section of its own, headed as exploratory. Give the numbers before the conclusions, and say what each conclusion rests on.
outputs: ANALYSIS.md: the planned analysis, then anything exploratory, each labeled

nodes.name: A critic reads the analysis
nodes.brief: Read the analysis beside the plan of record. Was each planned analysis run as written? Is everything else labeled exploratory? Does each conclusion follow from its numbers, and does the log explain every departure? You judge and do not rerun or rewrite. Verdict pass only when all four hold.
outputs: ANALYSIS-REVIEW.md: one line per point, and a verdict line

nodes.name: Write the report
nodes.brief: Write what was asked, what was planned before any data was seen, what was found, and what it does not show. Report the planned result whichever way it came out. Keep exploratory findings apart and call them that.

bar.name: A design that could fail
bar.acceptance: DESIGN.md says what is measured, on what and how many, and names the result that would count against the idea.

bar.name: The analysis that was planned
bar.acceptance: Every analysis in PREREGISTRATION.md is in ANALYSIS.md as planned, and everything else is labeled exploratory.
